agent_config.run_facts:
**This is a fitted campaign.** The first 284 sessions of the split are a FIT WINDOW: bars are delivered and your orders are ignored, exactly as during warmup, and your `fit()` is called once at the edge of it. You are scored on the remaining 100 sessions only, which you have never seen when `fit()` runs. You may define `fit`, `save_weights` and `load_weights` -- see section 7c of the API document above.

Fewer scored sessions means a noisier score: 100 against the 384 an unfitted campaign gets is roughly 1.96x the sampling error. That is arithmetic about the window, not a comment on your proposal.

Dataset: real NQ futures trades, 100 scored sessions on the pre-registered train split.

Fill model: unfavorable -- a fill requires a trade strictly through your limit, so you pay the spread on every entry and exit.

Commission: 0.1 index points per contract per side. NQ is $20 a point, so a round trip costs about $4.00 a contract. At high turnover this dominates: the baseline strategy on this split traded 103,355 times and paid more in commission than it made gross.

Action cap: 64 per session. History window: 512 bars.

record.note: MVP campaign, governed by docs/design/pre-registration.md. Real NQ train split. The model proposes one strategy at a time and edits the champion; the null is the sign-flip over round turns (section 3b), NOT the conditional null. The conditional null's FWER of 0.060 therefore does not describe this campaign; the figure that does is Task 57's, measured on this exact configuration at this exact N: 0 acceptances in 400 campaigns, FWER below about 0.010 at 95%. It is conservative, and Task 59 prices that -- 80% power at a signal strength of 0.287 against 0.242 for the conditional null.
record.stopping_rule: fixed budget; no early stop on any observed result
